two_sum.pyPYTHON 3
# A little logic. A new possibility.
def solve(nums, target):
seen = {}
for i, value in enumerate(nums):
complement = target - value
if complement in seen:
return [seen[complement], i]
seen[value] = i
return []

O(n) A better way forward.

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

A FEW GOOD
QUESTIONS.

More curious? Ask the CodeTrail guide.

Can I start with no coding experience?

Yes. Sign in to start learning. The Python course starts with the basics and moves through 16 modules. Lessons include explanations, examples, exercises, progressive hints and quizzes. Learn at your own pace.

Does it help with Meta and Microsoft interviews?

The course builds transferable coding, data-structure, algorithm and explanation skills, with timed mock practice. It is independent of Meta and Microsoft. Finishing the course or passing its tests does not guarantee a job or professional proficiency. Experienced roles can also require system design and behavioral preparation.

Can I practice Java too?

There is a Java basics track with an editor and code downloads. Java code does not compile or run in this workspace. The full 48-lesson course and in-browser test runner are for Python.

Is this a video course?

These are written, interactive lessons with worked examples and coding exercises, rather than prerecorded video lectures.

What is saved to my account?

Your lesson position, language selection, studied lessons, quiz progress, solved exercises and code drafts. Sign in and wait for the workspace to confirm saving. Tutor conversations can be saved through optional account memory; mock timers are not saved. Browser-only progress from an earlier version can be imported when offered.
